newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at record over 4,600 SMI.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at record over 4,600 SMI.

text.p: Swiss shares rose over one percent ON Thursday to end for the first time above 4,600 points on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), backed by a firmer dollar and Wall Street gains.
Dealers said the Swiss bourse tracked most European markets.
The long-term outlook remained good, although there was room for a correction in the near term after three says of advances.
"I am expecting the market to fall before there is another rise," one trader said.
SMI ended up 58.1 points or 1.28 percent at closing high of 4,605.2, narrowly below an all-time high of 4,609.4.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 34.82 points or 1.2 percent to 2,925.65.
Volume was heavy, pushed up by buy orders from abroad, one trader said.
The market was seen ignoring the rise in money market and swap rates as well as falling futures on Swiss government bonds, which has been a cause for concern in the bond market.
Dollar-sensitive industrials were in the limelight. Novartis registereds, which led the actives list, were among the biggest gainers with a gain of 37 francs to 1,747.
Share rights on Ciba Specialty Chemicals also added nearly two percent, gaining 1.75 francs to 10.75. Roche certificates were up 190 to 12,510.
ABB and Alusuisse posted gains of more than 1.5 percent each. ABB added 27 francs to 1,764, while Alusuisse climbed 22 francs to 1,212.
Among blue-chip financials, Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) was a clear winner. The stock ended at 299 francs, nine francs or 3.1 percent above Wednesday's close.
Dealers said the fact that SBC was the first of the Swiss major banks to announce sweeping changes in its provisions policy last year hightened expectations for the bank's 1996 results.
CS Group added 2.75 francs to a year high of 161. UBS bearers lost 13 francs to 1,327.
